# Acknowledgments {.unnumbered}

This book is built almost entirely on work other people gave away.

NCBI, EMBL-EBI, UniProt, the Protein Data Bank and the AlphaFold team run the
databases every chapter here depends on, and they serve them to anyone who asks
without charge and without an account. The authors who deposited the sequences,
the structures and the count matrices used in these pages had no obligation to
make them public. A book that costs the reader nothing is only possible because
of that.

The mammary gland dataset in Part 4 is GSE60450, deposited by the authors of a
2015 study of the switch to lactation. They were studying something else. Their
data is doing a job here they never planned for, which is the whole argument
for public deposition.

The Carpentries lessons, Rosalind, and the practitioners who write openly about
what actually goes wrong shaped how this book teaches. The debt is specific
rather than general: the exercise anatomy, the checkpoint placement, and the
decision to normalize errors before the reader's first one all came from
studying what those projects do.

The typefaces are open-licensed: Source Serif 4 from Adobe, Inter from Rasmus
Andersson, and JetBrains Mono from JetBrains. The book is written in Quarto and
typeset with LuaTeX.

**Technical review.** This edition has not yet been through independent
technical review. That's a real gap, and it's stated here rather than left for
a reader to discover. Every factual claim was checked against a live source
during production and the dates are in the dataset index, but checking your own
work isn't the same as somebody else checking it. If you have the expertise and
the inclination, the repository is open, and corrections are the most valuable
thing you can send.
